# The Explanation of the Noble Four Dharmas

Homage to Manjushri, the Youthful.

Why was this <term>sutra</term> <gloss>discourse</gloss> composed, which states that a <term>bodhisattva mahasattva</term> <gloss>great heroic being seeking awakening</gloss> should not abandon these four <term>dharmas</term> <gloss>qualities or principles</gloss> even for the sake of their life, as long as they live?

It was composed to correctly show the method for attaining unsurpassed awakening to those who are confused about how to enter the Great Vehicle correctly. It is also to cause those who are heedless to adopt it correctly, to encourage those who are discouraged, and to cause those who have entered correctly to rejoice.

The specific number four is mentioned to prevent the rejection of the teaching by those who might fear it is too vast and therefore not wish to listen. By stating the number, it is easily remembered. Furthermore, because the qualities of patience and gentleness, which appear below, serve a single purpose, they are not differentiated.

Although there are many categories of those who have correctly entered the Great Vehicle, two names <note>Bodhisattva and Mahasattva</note> are mentioned for three reasons: because of their interest, their application, and their understanding.

How is it through interest? They are called a <term>bodhisattva</term> <gloss>awakening-being</gloss> because of their interest in profound objects of knowledge. They are called a <term>mahasattva</term> <gloss>great being</gloss> because of their interest in great power.

How is it through application? Because they strive for the sake of their own unsurpassed, perfect awakening, and to completely protect all sentient beings from suffering.

How is it through understanding? Because awakening is realized through two powers. Which two? The power of intelligence and the power of diligence. One cannot realize awakening through ignorance or through small diligence.

### ON ALCHEMY

<margin>The end of Alchemy is not gold and silver, but secrets.</margin>
Who is there who would dare to deny that even in the best things a poison lies hidden and exists within? Everyone is compelled to confess this. If this is true, I now ask of you: should the poison not be separated from the good and the useful? And the good taken, and the evil left behind? Truly, it must be so. If it is necessary, then I ask you to tell me: how is that separation performed in your shops? For with you, everything remains mixed together. To protect your simplicity, if you are forced to confess that a poison lies hidden there and are asked where it eventually goes, you then bring forth I know not what regarding "corrections" which supposedly drive out and take away the poison,
<margin>Poison even in the best things.</margin>
just as they say <term>Cotonea</term> <gloss>quince</gloss> corrects <term>Scammonea</term> <gloss>scammony, a harsh purgative</gloss>, and later <term>Diagridium</term> <gloss>a preparation of scammony juice</gloss>. But what kind of correction is this? Does the poison not remain afterward just as it was at first? And yet you meanwhile boast that you have corrected it, so much so that the poison no longer harms. But where did it escape to?
<margin>The "correction" of physicians is examined.</margin>
It remains in the <term>Diagridium</term>. Test it, if you are wise: exceed the proper measure, and you will see where the poison is. For you shall know it without delay. Thus you also "correct" <term>Turbith</term> <gloss>a medicinal root</gloss> and call it <term>Diaturbith</term>. Such are your corrections, which would be fit for peasants and should be given to pack-horses. Make a trial by exceeding the limit and increase the dose: you shall see whether you do not feel the poison.
<margin>Diagridion.</margin>
*To correct is to take what has been corrected.* If someone is malicious and has sinned, and if he is punished, the correction extends no further than the will of the one who was punished lasts. Such are these corrections of yours; the power lies with the substances themselves, not with you. Now, in this case, a Physician must consider nothing further than that the poison be removed. This must be done through separation. For example: a serpent is poisonous, and yet it is adopted for food. If you remove the poison from it, you may eat it with no harm. The same is to be understood equally of all other things, namely that there is need for a similar separation. Until that is done, you cannot be secure in your operation—unless by chance it happens that nature supplies your deficiencies, or the greater benevolence of the heavens favors you. For in your art, no protection remains.
<margin>What "I correct a Physician" means.</margin>

Now at last, if that true foundation is required which takes away poison, let us see how Alchemy provides it. For it is necessary that it be done in this way: if Mars <note>the metal iron or the astrological influence</note> is in the Sun <note>gold or solar influence</note>, Mars must be removed; and if Saturn <note>lead or saturnine influence</note> is found in Venus <note>copper or venereal influence</note>, it must be separated from her. For as many ascendants and impressions as there are in the things of nature, so many bodies exist within them. Those bodies which are contrary must be entirely removed and taken away, so that in this way all contrariety is abolished, and the evil is taken from the good which you seek.
<margin>Fire perfects all things.</margin>
Just as gold is useful for nothing unless it is first cast into the fire, so a Medicine is much less useful which does not pass through the fire. For it is necessary for all things to pass through the fire into a second generation, by which they ought to benefit and help man. And should this not rightly be judged the upright foundation of any Physician? For a Physician ought not to apply poisons, but <term>arcana</term>.
<margin>The shops are rebuked.</margin>
However, all those official preparations in the shops, however many they may be, do not contribute a single letter to this doctrine. They are occupied simply in "correcting"—as if, if a dog farts in a chamber, that stench were suppressed either by <term>trochisci</term> <gloss>lozenges</gloss> and incense, or by juniper wood. I ask you: does the stench not remain in the room afterward just as before? And although it may not be perceived by smell, is it therefore lawful for anyone to say the stench has been separated and remains no longer? Indeed it is present, but "corrected" by the fumigation. Thus the fumigation and the foul air enter the nostrils together. Such also are the corrections of the Pharmacists, who blunt an <term>Aleopaticum</term> <note>a bitter or purgative medicine</note> with sugar, so that it inflicts no harm. Thus sugar and honey are their <term>magisterium</term> <gloss>mastery/sovereign remedy</gloss>. Thus they also "correct" gentian with <term>theriac</term> <gloss>a complex herbal jam used as an antidote</gloss>. Are these not the works of asinine ignorance? Yet they boast and sell themselves as the Physicians of princes. Who is so stupid that he does not immediately smell that these things are worthless? What else, I ask, can they boast about their remedies, except to say: *This Electuary is sweet, made of spices and sugar...*
